title: Classification table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Living things and their habitats (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from science/y6 lesson 9 (Classification table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 9: What is classification?. To understand why and how we classify things using their features

blocks.title: Sort into: Made of metal / Not metal
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Made of metal, Not metal.
blocks.answer: Made of metal: spoon; coin; key. Not metal: pencil; sock; cup

questions.q: Sort: robin, bee, bat, ant using 'has wings?'
questions.a: Wings: robin, bee, bat. No wings: ant (most ants).
questions.model: Ask the question for each one. Robin: wings, yes. Bee: yes. Bat: yes. Ant: worker ants have no wings. So three in one group, ant in the other.

questions.q: Why is 'is it big?' a poor question?
questions.a: People would disagree; it is an opinion, not a clear feature.
Sort into groups by shared features.

questions.q: Core: Collect 8 objects at home. Sort them two different ways and record both in tables.
questions.a: Pupils' own; e.g. by material and by use.
questions.model: Teacher shows one way first: by material (metal, plastic, fabric).

questions.q: Extend: Sort these animals with two questions: cat, eagle, goldfish, snake, frog, owl.
questions.a: For example: feathers? (eagle, owl); then fur? (cat); the rest: goldfish, snake, frog.

questions.q: Stretch: Why do scientists all over the world need the same system?
questions.a: So they can share findings and know they mean the same living thing.
A) a clear yes or no

questions.q: Big question: why do scientists sort living things into groups?
questions.a: To make millions of living things easier to name, study and compare.
